newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil net dlr inflows jump to $3.583 bln in July.
newsitem.headline: Brazil net dlr inflows jump to $3.583 bln in July.

text.p: Brazil's commercial and financial foreign exchange transactions soared to a preliminary surplus of $3.583 billion in July in the forex commercial market against a $814 million surplus in June, the Central Bank said.
It was the largest monthly surplus so far this year and was the result of a record $12.365 billion in financial buys in July, the Central Bank added.

Dealers said the large ammount of financial buys was due partly to the late June decision by the National Monetary Council (CMN), which allowed banks to invest money raised abroad for loans in dollar-indexed National Treasury Notes (NTN-D) prior to lending the money to firms.
Eurobond issues and cash paid for Brazilian privatizations also contributed to higher financial buys, dealers added.
While financial buy deals totalled $12.365 billion in July, financial sell operations amounted to $7.663 billion last month, according to the Central Bank.
The bank said July contracted exports totalled $4.599 billion and import operations totalled $5.718 billion.
